reviews.author: Graham W.
reviews.text:
We were pleasantly surprised by the 1 room camping cabin. As two adults who spent most daylight hours at others' campsites, it worked out nicely for sleep and storage.

The sleeping pads are more comfortable than they look, I didn't feel the need for any extra padding. In addition to bed linens, I would recommend also bringing your own curtains, as the supplied ones don't do much to block the morning light.

reviews.author: Jessi C.
reviews.text: This KOA is amazing! We experienced such friendly staff.  They continuously were busy around the campground,  making sure it was clean,  safe and making sure everything was running smoothly... and they always had a big smile on their faces and would wave greeting us everytime. The campground was really clean and the location is impeccable,  with the ocean being just a short walk across the street.  It's also close to several towns for supplies (although the store is fully stocked with anything you'd need as well) and so many beautiful trails.  We stayed in a cabin with 4 people. It was the perfect size,  very clean and nicely upkept,  and fully stocked.  We have older kids, and we still enjoyed the activities as a family,  with mini golf,  beanbags,  the pool/ hot tub and campfires! We highly recommend this location and we will be back!

reviews.author: Alex
reviews.text: We had an amazing stay at Warrenton / Seaside KOA Resort! Everything was great, clean, comfortable, and very family friendly. The staff was kind and helpful, and the atmosphere was wonderful. We enjoyed it so much that this is already our second time staying here, and we definitely want to come back again. Thank you for such a great experience!

reviews.author: Caitlin J.
reviews.text: This is the best campground! We have 7 and 9 year old kids and they were in heaven. The facility is top notch, super clean and you never run out of things to do with all the activities and ft Steven’s being right across the street. The staff are all extremely friendly and seem to love their jobs. We cannot wait to return! Take a bike ride through ft Steven’s to the shipwreck, you won’t be disappointed!

reviews.author: Korey
reviews.text: We booked a Kabin, which was clean but needs to be updated with some modern amenities (coffee maker, TV, complimentary items, etc.) and not rely totally on the location. We have stayed in many KOA locations, including one recently at Klamath Falls which was excellent, and this was on the lower end. Initially the service was great as we received an early check in notice text, but we could not reach a live person on the phone after making several attempts, although text messaging with another individual seemed to work fine.  This was not a concern when notifying the individual through text. Location is excellent for those wanting to visit nearby Astoria or the Lewis and Clark National Historical Park.

reviews.author: Andi E
reviews.text: They Charge $7.50 Per Person to anyone coming to visit you ? We had friends from Cannon Beach come by for 1 hr. They stoped them at the top and made each person in the car pay$7.50 each. RV spot about $120 a night for us plus all the hidden fees and then this. What a joke we were embarrassed and won't be back.

reviews.author: karlam902
reviews.text: We have a 5th wheel and booked a pull through site. What a great spot we got with trees, privacy, and lots of room. We would have extended our stay but couldn't keep our spot . Very nice people to work with and nice park. We wouldn't have liked it if we would have gotten a space below in big open area. But loved where we were. If we ever went back we would stay longer.

reviews.author: 269glennp
reviews.text: We stay here at least once a year over the past few years. The park has many good sites for big RVs like our 40 foot fifth wheel. The sites are always clean and fairly level and the patio sites are very well equiped with gas grill, swing, fire rings and cement patio. This resort would be a great choice for families as there are many choices for kids activities. One re-occuring problem has continued since our first visit in 2015 is the power surges. Power can spike at times up to 140 volts and without surge protection you could suffer damage to your electrical systems.

reviews.author: Luke G
reviews.text: Excellent place to camp with the kids. Lots of fun amenities and very friendly staff. The place is well kept and very clean. The Halloween festivities are a lot of fun. If you're there between April and October make sure to get some Gray's Comfort Q. One of the best brisket sandwiches I've ever had. Very tasty.

reviews.author: 2wheeltravelers2013
reviews.text: This was our first experience with this KOA, We booked for 3 nights over Memorial weekend but were slightly concerned how noisy it would be considering the large size of the park, this proved not to be the case considering the park was full. We stayed in one of the full hook up paved sites, which were large, beautifully maintained, with a degree of privacy without feeling hemmed in, and very quiet. The park was very clean and well kept; it has all of the amenities we you would come to expect to find in a good park. The staff are friendly and helpful. Definitely on our return list and a 'must stop' for the camper looking for a great experience.

reviews.author: Robert D
reviews.text: We stayed at the Astoria campground 10 days ago. It was raining. The campground was beautiful. What i did not like was the fact that the front desk acted like there was no room and tried to find a spot for our 40 ft RV and 12 ft trailer. We where 1 of 4 units in the whole campground (100 + sites for sure). What really got me upset was the fact they charged and $8.00 + tax on it for a resort fee. Everything was closed except the pool. So why a resort fee. I feel ripped off. The money won't kill me but it is the misrepresentation that bothers me. Not worth $58.00 a night. Better off at a roadside turn off. RD.

reviews.author: A Nichole K
reviews.text: I stayed at KOA Astoria this past weekend. This was my first time staying at a KOA. I was overall fine with the Deluxe Cabin setup (it was clean) and the staff was friendly. However, for a cost of $200+ per night was surprised that there were no reusable plates, bowls or utensils. To arrive to the cabin and have nothing reusable or microwave safe was shocking in 2024. Plastic cutlery and paper plates for the nightly cost is truly astonishing, also wasteful. Not to mention no dish soap or sponge were provided for use had I wished to wash the plastic utensils or any dishes I'd brought along. The "amenities" I experienced (mini golf area) were in need of some TLC, the putters could use replacements. I've done a lot of traveling to both private and larger run establishments in my lifetime and for a grand total of $412 for two nights was wildly unimpressed with the failure to provide otherwise cheap basics. I'd have spent my money elsewhere and had a better experience and will do so next time I'm in the area.

reviews.author: Jacqui I
reviews.text: This KOA is amazingly beautiful. The staff is amazing, polite, genuine and helpful. This KOA was extremely busy and the experience was fabulous with well cared for and clean facilities. The pancakes were free and fluffy. The pool and hot tub were clean and hot. The laundry room perfect and well priced. The shower was hot and clean. The check in process was friendly with professionalism. A few things to note: The KOA is a bit expensive with resort fee, site fee and pet fee its about $65 a night. Though, I think it is worth it. We will absolutely go back. Room tip: Pull thru site 20 was really nice; centrally located.

reviews.author: Becky Rufener
reviews.text: Easy check in, great stores, fabulous rv sites, super clean showers and bathrooms

reviews.author: Vicki Hager
reviews.text: Very nice place to stay. Very busy though. Quite the is pushed past its hours. Could use another restroom and shower facility centrally located. Have to be very careful driving through lots of kids that are not looking that will run out of nowhere.

reviews.author: Paul Weber
reviews.text: The only negative I can give you is the campsite (#129) assigned to us was a safety concern because most of the huge RV units going down or leaving at mid morning to the 300 section passed by us.
